definition: Grounding is an independently supplied directed relation on distinct basis, instance and inhabited fact tags. Soundness requires truth at both ends; asymmetry excludes reverse edges. It is not implication, quantification, or temporal production. Candidate-basis truth is fixed in the test, without an actual essence claim.
note: Minimal typed test for issue #273. Historical adoption or actual explanatory adequacy would require a further sourced argument; this encoding does not supply one.
